drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Counsel: Attached is a revised draft reflecting your proposed $450,000 Base Salary and 24-month severance structure, subject to our client’s approval. We have replaced the non-compete with confidentiality and trade-secret protections and added proposed good-reason mechanics for discussion. edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual Base Salary of $450,000, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices, and shall be eligible to participate in employee benefit plans under their applicable terms.
edits.name: Compensation

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. Upon termination by the Company without Cause or resignation by the Executive for Good Reason, the Company shall pay severance equal to 24 months of the Executive’s then-current Base Salary in substantially equal installments over 24 months, subject to applicable withholding and Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code. For that period, the Company shall also continue the Executive’s existing health and welfare benefits on substantially equivalent terms, to the extent permitted by applicable law and plan terms; if continuation is unavailable, the Company shall provide an economically equivalent payment, subject to applicable law. Good Reason means, without the Executive’s written consent, a material reduction in Base Salary, a material diminution in duties or authority, or relocation of the Executive’s principal workplace by more than 50 miles. The Executive must notify the Company within 60 days after the condition first occurs, allow 30 days to cure, and resign within 30 days after the cure period expires if the condition remains uncured. Cause means fraud, embezzlement, conviction of a felony involving dishonesty, willful misconduct materially harming the Company, or a material breach of this Agreement that remains uncured for 30 days after written notice, if curable.
edits.name: Severance and termination definitions

edits.text: 4. CONFIDENTIALITY AND TRADE SECRETS. No post-employment non-compete applies. The Executive shall not use or disclose the Company’s nonpublic confidential information except in performing duties for the Company or as authorized or required by law. These restrictions do not cover information that becomes public without breach, is lawfully received from an unrestricted third party, or is independently developed without use of confidential information, and do not restrict the Executive’s general skills and experience. Trade secrets remain protected for so long as they qualify as trade secrets under applicable law. Nothing prohibits reporting suspected violations of law to government authorities, cooperating with investigations, making legally protected disclosures, or exercising protected employment rights, and no prior authorization or notice is required. Under 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b), an individual is immune from liability under federal or state trade-secret law for confidential disclosure to a government official or attorney solely to report or investigate a suspected violation of law, or for disclosure in a complaint or other document filed under seal. An individual bringing a retaliation claim may disclose trade secrets to counsel and use them in the proceeding if filed under seal and otherwise disclosed only pursuant to court order.
edits.name: Replacement of non-compete
